questions.question: The Khilafat Movement was associated with which of the following communities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muslim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Khilafat Movement was initiated by the Muslim community in India in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I.
 
• It aimed to pressure the British government to preserve the sovereignty of the Ottoman Sultan, who was also regarded as the Caliph of Islam.
 
• Leaders such as Maulana Mohammad Ali and Maulana Shaukat Ali played pivotal roles in organizing and leading the movement.
 
• The Khilafat Movement was closely linked to the Indian freedom struggle and received support from Mahatma Gandhi as part of the Non-Cooperation Movement.
 
• The movement eventually declined by 1924 following the abolition of the Caliphate by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk in Turkey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ottoman Caliphate:** The Ottoman Caliphate was the Islamic Caliphate under the Ottoman Empire, symbolizing religious and political unity for Muslims.
 
• **World War I Impact:** The Ottoman Empire's defeat in World War I led to its partition, threatening the Caliphate's existence and prompting the Khilafat Movement.
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement:** Mahatma Gandhi supported the Khilafat Movement, integrating it into the broader struggle against British colonial rule in India.
 
• **Decline of the Movement:** The abolition of the Caliphate by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk in 1924 marked the end of the Khilafat Movement.
 
• **Legacy:** While the movement did not achieve its goal, it strengthened Hindu-Muslim unity temporarily and contributed to India's independence movement.

questions.question: Who is the Cabinet Secretary of India as of September 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__TV Somanathan__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• T. V. Somanathan (born 10 May 1965) is an Indian bureaucrat and IAS officer who is serving as the Cabinet Secretary of India since 30 August 2024. 
 
• Before this, he served as the Finance Secretary of India (Department of Expenditure).
 
• Prior to this appointment, he served as Additional Secretary and Joint Secretary in the Prime Minister's Office (PMO).
 
• He also worked as Director at the World Bank Group, Washington D.C., where he initially joined under its Young Professionals Program.
 
• He is a 1987 batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Tamil Nadu cadre.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role of the Cabinet Secretary:**

 
 
• Acts as the principal coordinator between the Union Government and various ministries/departments.
 
• Heads the Cabinet Secretariat and facilitates decision-making at the highest level of governance.
 
• Advises the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers on policy matters and administrative decisions.
 
 
 
• **Appointment Process:**
 
 
• The Cabinet Secretary is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), chaired by the Prime Minister.
 
• The tenure is generally fixed at two years, but extensions can be granted based on performance and necessity.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The post of Cabinet Secretary was established in 1950, with N. R. Pillai being the first to hold the position.
 
• It is considered the apex post in the Indian civil service hierarchy.
 
 
 
• **Cabinet Secretariat:**
 
 
• It functions as the administrative arm of the Cabinet and handles major inter-ministerial coordination.
 
• It ensures smooth communication and implementation of decisions taken by the Union Council of Ministers.

questions.question: What change was observed in agricultural practices after the Green Revolution?

options.text: Focus on monoculture of wheat only
Decrease in the use of fertilisers
Shift from low-yield to high-yield crops
Shift from cash crops to subsistence farming

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shift from low-yield to high-yield crops**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India, initiated in the 1960s, led to a significant shift from **traditional low-yield crops** to high-yield varieties (HYVs) of crops, particularly wheat and rice.
 
• The introduction of HYVs was complemented by the use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and advanced irrigation techniques to enhance agricultural productivity.
 
• It resulted in a dramatic increase in food grain production, especially in states like Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh, transforming India from a food-deficient country to a food-surplus one.
 
• The focus was primarily on staple crops like wheat and rice, which were scientifically bred to produce higher yields, ensuring food security and reducing dependency on imports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High-Yield Varieties (HYVs):** These are genetically modified crops designed to produce higher yields than traditional varieties, requiring intensive use of fertilizers and irrigation.
 
• **Irrigation Techniques:** The Green Revolution encouraged the adoption of modern irrigation methods like canal systems and tube wells to ensure adequate water supply for crops.
 
• **Fertilizers and Pesticides:** Chemical fertilizers and pesticides became integral to the success of the Green Revolution, aiding in pest control and providing essential nutrients to crops.
 
• **Impact on Economy:** The increased agricultural output contributed to a rise in rural incomes, reduced poverty in certain regions, and boosted India's economic growth during the late 20th century.
 
• **Criticism of Monoculture:** While the Green Revolution improved food security, it also led to environmental issues like soil degradation, water scarcity, and loss of biodiversity due to the focus on monoculture farming.

questions.question: Which outcome is typically expected from a government's expansionary fiscal policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Stimulation of economic growth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Expansionary fiscal policy involves increasing government spending or reducing taxes to boost **aggregate demand** in the economy.
 
• The primary goal is to stimulate **economic growth**, especially during periods of economic slowdown or recession.
 
• By increasing public expenditure, the government encourages **job creation** and higher consumer spending.
 
• Tax cuts leave individuals and businesses with more disposable income, further fueling **consumption and investment.**
 
• This policy often leads to a **temporary rise in the fiscal deficit**, which is offset by the long-term economic benefits of growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Policy:**

 
 
• Fiscal policy refers to the use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy.
 
• It is categorized into two types: **expansionary** and **contractionary** fiscal policy.
 
 
 
• **Aggregate Demand:**
 
 
• Aggregate demand is the total demand for goods and services within an economy at a given overall price level and time.
 
• It includes consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports.
 
 
 
• **Multiplier Effect:**
 
 
• Increased government spending can have a multiplier effect, where the initial spending leads to multiple rounds of increased economic activity.
 
• This amplifies the overall impact of fiscal measures on GDP growth.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Expansionary fiscal policy can lead to **inflationary pressures** if the economy is already operating near its capacity.
 
• It may increase the government's **debt levels** if not managed prudently.

questions.question: A very heavy concentration of Malwa settlements of Chalcolithic period was found in the:
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Central Narmada Basin is one of the richest regions in terms of Chalcolithic settlements, particularly those belonging to the Malwa culture.
 
• Malwa settlements are characterized by advanced pottery styles, including painted pottery with intricate designs.
 
• Excavations in this region have revealed evidence of agricultural practices, including the cultivation of wheat and barley.
 
• The sites in the Central Narmada Basin include significant findings such as tools made of copper and stone, indicating a transitional phase between the Stone Age and Metal Age.
 
• Prominent Chalcolithic sites in this region include Navdatoli and Daimabad, which provide insights into the socio-economic aspects of the Malwa culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chalcolithic Period:** The Chalcolithic period refers to the phase of human history where copper began to be used alongside stone tools.
 
• **Malwa Culture:** This culture is one of the prominent Chalcolithic cultures in India, known for its distinctive painted pottery and advanced agricultural practices.
 
• **Navdatoli:** A key Chalcolithic site located near the Narmada River, offering evidence of early settlement patterns, agricultural activity, and craft production.
 
• **Daimabad:** A significant site in Maharashtra linked to the Malwa culture, known for its discovery of bronze artifacts including the famous "Bronze Chariot."
 
• **Geographical Significance:** The Narmada Basin provided fertile land, water resources, and access to raw materials, making it suitable for early human settlements and the growth of Chalcolithic cultures.

questions.question: How many points are awarded for Lona in Kabaddi?

• In Kabaddi, a **Lona** is awarded when the entire opposing team is declared out.
 
• A Lona in Kabaddi fetches the team **2 additional points** apart from the points scored for individual outs.
 
• The concept of Lona encourages teams to strategize and attempt to eliminate all the opposing players.
 
• The awarded 2 points for a Lona can play a crucial role in deciding the final outcome of the match, especially in close contests.

• **Kabaddi**:

 
 
• Kabaddi is a contact team sport originating from India and is now popular worldwide, particularly in South Asia.
 
• The game is played between two teams of seven players each, and the objective is to score points by raiding the opponent’s half and tagging players.
 
• Players must chant "Kabaddi" continuously during a raid to demonstrate controlled breathing.
 
 
 
• **Point System in Kabaddi:**
 
 
• Each player tagged by the raider earns the raider's team 1 point.
 
• Bonus points are awarded when specific conditions are met, such as crossing a bonus line during a raid.
 
• The defensive team earns points by successfully tackling the raider (known as a super tackle if done with 3 or fewer defenders).

• Teams often attempt to eliminate all opposing players for a strategic advantage.

questions.question: What does the Greek letter ν (nu) represent in physics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Frequency of a wave**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Greek letter **ν (nu)** is commonly used in physics to denote the **frequency of a wave**, particularly in the context of electromagnetic waves and sound waves.
 
• Frequency is defined as the **number of oscillations or cycles per unit of time**, usually measured in Hertz (Hz), where 1 Hz equals 1 cycle per second.
 
• The relationship between the speed of a wave (v), its frequency (ν), and wavelength (λ) is given by the equation: **v = ν × λ**.
 
• In quantum mechanics, ν is also used to represent the frequency of photons, which is related to their energy by the equation **E = hν**, where h is Planck's constant.
 
• The symbol ν should not be confused with similar Greek letters like μ (mu), which represents different physical quantities such as permeability or reduced mass.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frequency (ν):** Frequency is a fundamental property of waves, describing how often the wave oscillates. It is inversely proportional to the period (T) of the wave, where **ν = 1/T**.
 
• **Hertz (Hz):** The SI unit of frequency, named after Heinrich Hertz, where 1 Hz equals 1 cycle per second.
 
• **Wave Equation:** The wave equation **v = ν**× **× λ** establishes a relationship between the speed of the wave (v), its frequency (ν), and its wavelength (λ).
 
• **Applications of Frequency:** Frequency plays a crucial role in various fields, including telecommunications (radio and TV signals), acoustics (sound waves), and quantum mechanics (photon energy).
 
• **Planck's Equation:** In quantum mechanics, the energy of a photon is directly proportional to its frequency, represented by the equation **E = hν**, where h = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s (Planck's constant).

questions.question: Right to constitutional remedies as a Fundamental Right of the Constitution of India is stated in which of the following Articles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution provides the right to constitutional remedies, empowering citizens to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of their Fundamental Rights.
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar referred to Article 32 as the "heart and soul" of the Indian Constitution as it guarantees the protection of Fundamental Rights.
 
• Under Article 32, the Supreme Court can issue writs such as habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto, and certiorari to enforce rights.
 
• This article ensures that no individual’s Fundamental Rights are violated without legal recourse.
 
• Article 32 is applicable only when there is a violation of Fundamental Rights, making it a cornerstone of judicial review in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights:** Enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution, these rights are guaranteed to all citizens and include rights such as equality, freedom, and protection from exploitation.
 
• **Types of Writs:** The writs issued under Article 32 include habeas corpus (protection against unlawful detention), mandamus (commanding public authority to perform its duty), prohibition (preventing lower courts from exceeding jurisdiction), certiorari (quashing orders of inferior courts), and quo warranto (challenging the legality of a public office).
 
• **Judicial Review:** Article 32 underlines the concept of judicial review, which allows the judiciary to ensure that laws and executive actions do not violate Fundamental Rights.
 
• **Supreme Court’s Role:** Article 32 exclusively empowers the Supreme Court to be the guardian of Fundamental Rights, though High Courts can enforce these rights under Article 226.
 
• **Article 226:** While Article 32 applies to the Supreme Court, Article 226 allows High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights as well as other legal rights.

questions.question: How many types of plate tectonic boundaries are there?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• There are **three types of plate tectonic boundaries**: divergent, convergent, and transform boundaries.
 
• **Divergent boundaries** occur when plates move apart, leading to the formation of new crust (e.g., mid-ocean ridges).
 
• **Convergent boundaries** occur when plates collide, often resulting in mountain formation or subduction zones (e.g., Himalayas or Mariana Trench).
 
• **Transform boundaries** occur when plates slide past one another horizontally, causing earthquakes (e.g., San Andreas Fault).
 
• These boundaries are driven by the movement of tectonic plates due to **mantle convection, slab pull, and ridge push**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tectonic Plates:** Large sections of Earth's lithosphere divided into rigid plates that float on the semi-fluid asthenosphere below.
 
• **Mid-Ocean Ridges:** Underwater mountain ranges formed at divergent boundaries, where magma rises to create new crust.
 
• **Subduction Zones:** Areas where one plate is forced beneath another at convergent boundaries, often causing volcanic activity.
 
• **Earthquakes:** Commonly associated with transform boundaries, where stress builds up as plates move past each other.
 
• **Plate Movement Drivers:** Mantle convection (heat-driven fluid motion), slab pull (gravity pulling a subducting plate), and ridge push (force exerted by magma at divergent boundaries) are key mechanisms behind plate tectonics.

• Kathakali combines elements of dance, music, and acting, rooted in themes from **Indian epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana**.

questions.question: No money bill can be introduced in the State Legislative Assembly without the prior permission of the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A Money Bill can only be introduced in the State Legislative Assembly **with the prior permission of the Governor**.
 
• As per Article 207 of the Constitution of India, the Governor's recommendation is mandatory for introducing Money Bills in the State Legislature.
 
• The Money Bill deals with matters such as the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration, or regulation of taxes, borrowing of money by the state, and matters related to the Consolidated Fund of the State.
 
• The Governor acts as the formal authority for legislative proposals involving state finances, ensuring they align with constitutional provisions.
 
• Without the Governor's recommendation, a Money Bill cannot proceed in the legislative process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Money Bill:**

 
 
• It is defined under Article 110 of the Indian Constitution (at the Union level) and Article 199 (at the State level).
 
• A Money Bill exclusively deals with financial matters like taxation, appropriation of funds, and public expenditure.
 
• It can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha (Union) or State Legislative Assembly (State) and requires prior recommendation from the President (Union) or Governor (State).
 
 
 
• **Role of the Governor:**
 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• In financial matters, the Governor ensures compliance with constitutional provisions by granting or withholding consent for legislative proposals.
 
 
 
• **State Legislature:**
 
 
• It comprises the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and, in some states, the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).
 
• The Legislative Assembly is the lower house where Money Bills are introduced and deliberated upon.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Process for Money Bills:**
 
 
• A Money Bill, after being introduced in the Legislative Assembly with the Governor's consent, goes through a detailed legislative process including debate, approval, and assent.
 
• The Legislative Council, if present, can only make recommendations and cannot amend or reject a Money Bill.
 
• After approval, it requires the Governor's assent to become law.

questions.question: The smallest natural number which is divisible by 33, 72, 11 and 18 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The required number must be divisible by 72, which means it must be a multiple of 9.

Using the divisibility rule of 9 (sum of digits must be divisible by 9) on the given options:

⇒ 881 → 8 + 8 + 1 = 17 | 839 → 8 + 3 + 9 = 20 | 696 → 6 + 9 + 6 = 21 (None are divisible by 9)

⇒ 792 → 7 + 9 + 2 = 18 (Divisible by 9)

Since only 792 is a multiple of 9, we can eliminate all other options instantly.

**∴ The correct answer is 792.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 33, 72, 11, and 18.

**Method Used:**

The smallest natural number completely divisible by all given numbers is their Least Common Multiple (LCM).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 33 = 3 × 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 72 = 2³ × 3²

⇒ Prime factorization of 11 = 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 18 = 2 × 3²

⇒ LCM = Highest powers of all prime factors present

⇒ LCM = 2³ × 3² × 11

⇒ LCM = 8 × 9 × 11

⇒ LCM = 72 × 11

⇒ LCM = 792

**∴ The correct answer is 792.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by each of the given numbers. It is obtained by multiplying the highest powers of all prime factors present in the numbers.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The largest positive integer that divides all the given numbers without leaving a remainder. It is the product of the lowest powers of common prime factors.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is perfectly divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 9.

Divisibility Rule of 11
